claims.claim: Engine oil pump balance shaft assembly for Toyota cars (e.g., Camry 2018–present, RAV4).
claims.evidence: Witness photos show a generic metal gearbox/transmission-like assembly with shafts/bolts and stamped markings, but no readable Toyota fitment, part number, or clear identification of an oil pump/balance shaft.
No documentation, labels, shipping marks, or serial/part-number plate readable in the witness photos.
Photos only show the unit lying on concrete with visible residue; there is no running/test footage or diagnostic printout.
No tamper evidence, seal marks, or mileage/usage records are visible/readable in the witness photos.

risks.risk: Wrong part type/fitment: photos look like a gearbox/transmission assembly, not clearly an oil pump/balance shaft; could be incompatible with the stated Toyota models.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the exact part name/label/part number plate (or stamped code) and a photo showing the mating interface that matches the Toyota application.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a generic used transmission/gearbox-type assembly with unknown compatibility (worst-case: may not fit or may be incomplete).

risks.risk: Internal condition unknown (wear, play, damaged bearings/gears) despite “no knock” claim; photos cannot confirm internal wear.
risks.proof: Video clip of the unit being spun/bench-tested (showing smooth rotation) and/or a short sound recording demonstrating “no knock,” plus close-ups of bearing/gear contact areas if accessible.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not proven working (worst-case: may have internal wear or noise).

risks.risk: Leakage/contamination: oil/grease residue is visible; could indicate leaks, seal failure, or prior damage.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all seals/gaskets and any wet spots after wiping, plus a clip showing whether fresh oil appears after a short run or time on a clean surface.
risks.if_unproven: Price as potentially leaking/needs reseal (worst-case: seals/gaskets replacement required).

risks.risk: Completeness risk: photos don’t show whether all internal components and required mounting hardware are included.
risks.proof: A full laid-out inventory photo/clip showing all included parts (linkages, bolts, seals, brackets) and a photo of the full assembly from multiple angles confirming nothing missing.
risks.if_unproven: Price as incomplete/unknown completeness (worst-case: missing parts reduce value).

risks.risk: Condition damage risk: cracks, stripped threads, bent shafts, or casing damage may not be visible in the limited angles.
risks.proof: High-resolution photos of the entire casing, all threaded studs/bolt holes, and shaft ends from straight-on and angled views; include a close-up of any stamped markings and edges.
risks.if_unproven: Price as used with possible cosmetic/structural defects (worst-case: damage affecting installation or durability).

proof_requests: Send a clear photo of the exact part number/label/stamp that identifies it as an oil pump/balance shaft assembly (not just a gearbox-like housing).
Provide a photo showing the mating interface and how it mounts to the Toyota engine/transmission area (fitment proof).
Share a short bench-test video: demonstrate smooth rotation and/or show “no knock” with sound.
Show close-ups of seals/gaskets and any leak points; wipe test (clean surface then show if fresh residue appears).
Confirm completeness: list and photograph every included accessory/hardware and show the full assembly from all sides.
response.reason: The witness photos confirm a metal transmission/gearbox-like assembly but do not clearly verify the seller’s specific claim (oil pump/balance shaft) or Toyota fitment, nor do they prove working/test status. Without an identifying part number/label and test evidence, pricing would be too speculative.
